A Rather Long Title That Needs To Be Wrapped Over More Than One Line On
             The First Page Of The Rendered Draft Document
                         draft-example-rich-07

Abstract

   This abstract has code, a reference to [RFC8555] and two sentences.
   Here is the second one, which is long enough to wrap on to another
   line of the output text.

Status of This Memo

   This Internet-Draft is submitted in full conformance with the
   provisions of BCP 78 and BCP 79.

   Internet-Drafts are working documents of the Internet Engineering
   Task Force (IETF).  Note that other groups may also distribute
   working documents as Internet-Drafts.  The list of current Internet-
   Drafts is at https://datatracker.ietf.org/drafts/current/.

   Internet-Drafts are draft documents valid for a maximum of six months
   and may be updated, replaced, or obsoleted by other documents at any
   time.  It is inappropriate to use Internet-Drafts as reference
   material or to cite them other than as "work in progress."

   This Internet-Draft will expire on 28 April 2027.

1.  Introduction

   Plain text with _emphasis_, *strong text* and a link
   (https://example.com/a?b=1&c=2).  A sentence ending in e.g. an
   abbreviation.  Dr. Example said so.  See [HANDBOOK], [AVERYLONGLABEL]
   and [REGISTRY]; also https://example.com/some/path/that-is/long-
   enough/to/need/a/break/somewhere/in/the/middle/of/it.

   Section references come in three forms: [RFC8555], Section 7.3,
   Section 8.1 of [RFC8555] and [RFC8555] (Appendix A.1).  See also
   Section 3.1, Appendix A, Appendix A.1 and Appendix "Acknowledgments".
   Is this a question?  Yes!  It is -- or is it--really.

2.  Conventions and Definitions

   The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT",
   "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and
   "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in
   BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all
   capitals, as shown here.




Example, et al.           Expires 28 April 2027                 [Page 2]

Internet-Draft                    RICH                      October 2026


3.  Requirements and Lists With a Section Title That Is Long Enough to
    Wrap in Both the Body and the Table of Contents

   A client MUST do this, SHOULD NOT do that, and MAY do the other.

   *  first item

   *  second item, which MUST NOT be skipped and which is long enough
      that it has to continue on a second line of text

3.1.  Nested Lists

   1.   Step one

        *  Detail with a formula:

           a < b && b > c

           -  a sub-detail

           -  another, with an empty object ({})

        *  Second detail

   2.   Step two

   3.   Step three

   4.   Step four

   5.   Step five

   6.   Step six

   7.   Step seven

   8.   Step eight

   9.   Step nine

   10.  Step ten, in a list wide enough for two digits, with enough text
        to wrap around to the following line

   11.  Step eleven

   Example record:

       "value" )

   Example object:

   { "a": [1, 2, 3],
           "tabbed": true }
